Candidates for the rule (trailing "not X" / "rather than X" clauses):

1. "Field crews still collect vouchers, make no mistake." This is not an antonym trailer, so it is left alone.
2. "is not merely academic—it is essential" is not a trailing clause, so it is left alone.
3. "Breeders select dwarfing alleles on purpose, rather than by accident." This is an ordinary-knowledge antonym, so the trailer is cut.
4. "Conservation collections still accession landraces, rather than heirlooms." Landraces versus heirlooms is a genuine, domain-specific distinction that is tacked on. The rule says to flag uncertain cases, but this one clearly falls on the genuine side. Rewriting it would mean inventing facts about what the collections do (Rule 12 accuracy), so I flag it for the author.
5. "The construct was designed for chloroplast transformation, not nuclear transformation." This is a genuine distinction that is tacked on, and a rewrite would require inventing detail, so I flag it.
6. "Morphine is not synthesized by the Pacific yew; it is produced in Papaver somniferum latex." This is a separate sentence, not a trailer, so it is left alone.
7. "Herbarium staff still mark sterile Carex sheets as undetermined… until a fruiting collection arrives." This has no antonym trailer.
8. "Rubisco is the only carboxylase in the Calvin-Benson cycle, full stop." This has no antonym trailer.
